Definition: from G1909 and G142; to raise up (literally or figuratively):--exalt self, poise (lift, take) up.
BiblicalUsage: To lift up, to raise. Men are to pray everywhere lifting up holy hands in 1 Timothy 2:8, Jesus tells the disciples to lift up their eyes on the fields white for harvest in John 4:35, and He was taken up before their eyes in Acts 1:9. But the word also warns: every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God must be cast down in 2 Corinthians 10:5.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe lifting up is the posture of the Christian life — hands lifted in prayer, eyes lifted to the harvest, and every proud thought brought low. I hold that what I lift up to God, He lifts up in blessing, and what exalts itself against Him will fall.
